title: What If a City Banned Cars Every Sunday? Bogotá Has Since 1974

description:
What if a capital city closed its streets to cars every single Sunday? Bogotá, Colombia, has done it since the first Ciclovía on 15 December 1974, when about 5,000 cyclists took over more than 100 blocks; the city made it an official programme in 1976.
Today more than 120 km of streets are closed to cars every Sunday and public holiday from 7am to 2pm, and an estimated 1.7 million people take part each week. Bogotá's cycling share rose from 0.58 percent of trips in 1998 to about 9 percent by 2019, on a permanent network now approaching 600 km of bike lanes. Nearly 500 cities hold a Ciclovía-style event at least twice a year, but cost has kept major US cities from closing streets weekly.
